facts: The interior angle and the exterior angle of a sector add to $360^{\circ}$.
The interior angle is the one **inside** the sector, so check which region the arc sits in before using a marked number.
A quadrant has an interior angle of $90^{\circ}$, and a semicircle has an interior angle of $180^{\circ}$.
steps: If an angle is given, decide whether it is the interior or the exterior angle of the sector.
If the marked angle is inside the sector, use it directly. If it is outside the sector, subtract it from $360^{\circ}$ to find the interior angle.
State the interior angle in degrees.

workedExamples.solution_text:
a) The marked $83^{\circ}$ angle is outside the sector.
$\text{interior} = 360^{\circ} - 83^{\circ}$
$= 277^{\circ}$
b) The marked $277^{\circ}$ angle is outside the sector.
$\text{interior} = 360^{\circ} - 277^{\circ}$
$= 83^{\circ}$

development.solution_text:
The arc of the marked angle lies in the unshaded region, outside the sector, so $80^{\circ}$ is the exterior angle.
$\theta = 360^{\circ} - 80^{\circ}$
$= 280^{\circ}$

The arc marking $240^{\circ}$ sweeps through the unshaded region, so $240^{\circ}$ is the exterior angle, not the angle inside the sector.
$\theta = 360^{\circ} - 240^{\circ}$
$= 120^{\circ}$
